subject.title: feat: per-job elevated exec scoping for cron and heartbeat

question: Should elevated cron and heartbeat authority be solved as a narrow per-job/heartbeat marker now, or folded into the broader Gateway-owned scheduling provenance design?
rationale: The choice defines who may create, preserve, modify, and inherit host-elevated execution authority across persisted schedules and autonomous heartbeat runs, which is a security and upgrade contract rather than a mechanical fix.

options.title: Fold Into Provenance Design
options.body: Make the broader scheduling provenance work explicitly cover per-job elevated authority, heartbeat modification provenance, audit receipts, execution lineage, and migration semantics.

options.title: Implement Narrow Elevated Marker
options.body: Add a focused per-job and heartbeat authority marker now, with tests and docs for create, update, execution, and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Fail Closed First
options.body: Disable elevated execution for internal cron and heartbeat senders by default until maintainers approve a durable provenance model, accepting compatibility disruption.

recommendation.title: Fold Into Provenance Design
recommendation.body: Make the broader scheduling provenance work explicitly cover per-job elevated authority, heartbeat modification provenance, audit receipts, execution lineage, and migration semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: They most recently owned the merged cron caller-scope boundary that this elevated provenance decision builds on.
